full_judgment:
This Rule calls in question an order of remand dated 11.2.1986 passed by the 1st Commercial Court of the Subordinate Judge, Chittagong in Other Appeal No. 199 after 1985 after setting aside the judgment and decree for ejectment of monthly tenant passed by the Munsif, 1st Court, Chittagong dated 28.2.1985 in Other Suit No. 308 of 1979. 

 4. The learned Munsif decreed the suit on contest with cost by the judgment and decree as aforesaid. Against the said decree the defendant preferred an appeal and the learned appellate court by the impugned judgment and order set aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif and remanded the suit for rehearing in the light of some observation made in the judgment on the point of service of notice though affirmed all other findings of the learned Munsif. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of remand the plaintiff obtained the present Rule. 

 7. On the point of service of notice of termination of tenancy the learned Munsif found that one notice by registered cover Exts 6 (a) was sent to the town address of the defendant which was returned to the plaintiff with remark "refused". Another was sent by registered cover Ext. 6 sent to the village address of the defendant which was re-directed to his town address and it was returned to the plaintiff with remarks refused". With the aforesaid observations the learned Munsif found that the notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was duly served on the defendant terminating the tenancy. The learned Subordinate Judge, on that point, observed that Ext. 6 does not indicate that it was re-directed and so it cannot be treated as such. As regard Ext. G(a), the notice sent to the town address of the defendant, the learned appellate Court found that the endorsement "refused" is not written there. But it bears the remark ''not claimed". Hence he remanded the suit for fresh trial after verification of service of Ext. 6 and 6(a) by a man of the postal department and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif. 

 9. Mr. Syed Md. Ali, the learned Advocate submits that as the Rule was issued against the order of remand and not against any decree, in the fitness of things, the appeal should be remanded for re-hearing to enable the learned appellate court to come to a correct decision on the question of fact in the light of the observation of this court instead of deciding the matter finally as the entire matter is not before this court but the order of remand and this court in exercise of the jurisdiction u/s. 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot reverse a finding of fact. 

 12. Hence it is clear that no distinction has been made in that section between the order or orders of remand and decree and this court may pass any order as it thinks fit in Revision. It is to be maintained that it is an established principle of law that if a finding of fact is based on misreading and misconstruction of the evidence on record or is contrary to the evidence on record it may be reversed in revision u/s 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The submission of Mr. Ali, therefore, has no substance. 

 13. In the instant case the learned appellate court affirmed all the findings of the learned Munsif save and except finding of service of notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act and I have already found that the learned appellate court committed an error of law in holding that the service was not proved and I have further found that it is duly served as apparent from the papers filed as was found by the learned Munsif. Hence I am of the opinion that no fruitful purpose will be served by remanding the appeal which will simply delay the final disposal of the matter. So the decree passed by the learned Munsif should be upheld. 

 14. In this view of the matter the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The judgment and order complained of are set aside and the Other Appeal No. 199 of 1985 is dismissed without cost and the judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif are restored.
